rationale: The immediate issue is too many simultaneous active roles may leave no perceptual foreground or rest. The first experiment tests that explanation while protecting against level, source, arrangement, processing, and monitoring confounds.

recommended_first_experiment.action: Mute one nonessential layer at a time in the busiest section and keep the first removal that improves focus without creating a hole.
recommended_first_experiment.summary: Mute one nonessential layer at a time in the busiest section and keep the first removal that improves focus without creating a hole.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: It changes one high-information variable and can strengthen or weaken competing explanations before a permanent treatment.

starting_points: Change one arrangement dimension at a time: role, entrance/exit, density, register, rhythm, note length, or focal hierarchy.
Make structural edits in a Project Alternative or duplicated region so comparison and recovery remain exact.
Judge through the transition and full section; a momentary solo is not enough to evaluate form or focus.
stop_rule: Stop when the focal role, section purpose, and transition are clear and another change no longer adds a distinct musical function.
teaching_principle: Arrangement allocates listener attention across time; remove or redirect competing roles before asking mixing tools to manufacture clarity.
title: How do I know when an arrangement is too dense
tradeoffs_and_risks: Simplification can improve focus while reducing desired scale, texture, or genre energy.
More contrast can make transitions feel disconnected if no identity cue carries across.
Register or voicing changes can alter harmony, performance, or emotional meaning.
undo_or_reset: Restore the preserved regions, mutes, levels, voicings, automation, or project alternative and replay the same section.

what_to_listen_for: The focal element and section purpose should become easier to understand without losing the song’s identity or intended energy.
The next transition or arrival should gain contrast rather than merely becoming louder or busier.
Removed or changed layers should have a named consequence; keep them out if no meaningful role is lost.
Explicitly preserve: energy, genre character.

rationale: The immediate issue is synth harmonics and sustained envelope may occupy the focal vocal region continuously. The first experiment tests that explanation while protecting against level, source, arrangement, processing, and monitoring confounds.

recommended_first_experiment.action: Move the synth response into gaps, reduce activity, or dynamically duck a focused band only during vocal lines.
recommended_first_experiment.summary: Move the synth response into gaps, reduce activity, or dynamically duck a focused band only during vocal lines.
recommended_first_experiment.why_this_first: It changes one high-information variable and can strengthen or weaken competing explanations before a permanent treatment.

starting_points: Test level, register/voicing, timing, note length, and arrangement role before carving permanent spectral holes.
When EQ is justified, begin broad and modest—often about 1–2 dB as a diagnostic move—then level-match and adjust by ear.
Use dynamic processing only when the collision is demonstrably intermittent and preserve tone between events.
stop_rule: Stop or back off when the target cue becomes clear but the supporting source loses useful body, character, blend, or mono stability.
teaching_principle: Create space around the vocal’s important cues in the competing source and only when needed; do not hollow out every instrument permanently.
title: A lead or pad synth keeps swallowing the singer. How do I allocate the midrange
tradeoffs_and_risks: Creating spectral space can remove useful body, blend, realism, or source identity.
Dynamic or multiband methods add timing, crossover, and detector complexity.
Stereo separation may collapse in mono and does not solve center masking reliably.
undo_or_reset: Restore the preserved regions, mutes, levels, voicings, automation, or project alternative and replay the same section.
user_language_aliases: synth harmonics and sustained envelope may occupy the focal vocal region continuously
what_to_listen_for: The obscured cue—pitch, lyric, attack, body, rhythm, or texture—should become clearer in the full mix.
The supporting source should retain enough body, character, and role rather than sounding hollow or disconnected.
The improvement should survive matched loudness and, where relevant, mono or small-speaker checks.
Explicitly preserve: synth identity, vocal clarity.
